Highest-burden core. Four counties are flagged as high-burden by all five nationally-available sources (Tier 1): Williamsburg County SC, Lea County NM, Pike County KY, Sullivan County NY. A further 147 counties are flagged by four sources (Tier 2) — dominated by Great Plains reservation counties (Buffalo/Dewey/Corson SD, Blaine MT, Benson ND, Thurston NE) and Texas/New-Mexico oil-and-border counties (McMullen, Dimmit, Wheeler, Live Oak TX; Union NM).

How cumulative burden is scored

Count stressors (EPA facilities, federal court cases, treatment providers) are normalized per 10,000 residents, ranked into national percentiles, and flagged in the worst national tertile. A county's cross-source agreement (0–5) counts how many of five independent stressor sources flag it: many facilities, high social vulnerability, high federal-court activity, nonmetro rurality (RUCC ≥ 4), and treatment-service scarcity. The burden index (0–1) is the mean of the five stressor percentiles. Read agreement as primary; the index breaks ties.

Burden × source, and the highest-burden counties

Each cell = a county's national percentile on that stressor; rows are the 30 highest-agreement counties. Blank service-scarcity cells = counties with no mapped substance-use-treatment providers at all.
Top 25 counties by cross-source agreement, then composite burden index.

Findings by entity type

Places (spatial backbone). spatialkg supplies the S2 Level-13 grid and GADM county/state hierarchy (FIPS + geometry) for the contiguous U.S.; spoke-okn resolves ~42,700 ZIPs and ~27,500 places, with PARTOF_LpL linking place→county — the join that makes county-level health aggregation possible.
Environmental burden. regulatory 3.6 M facility-county records (162,254 PFAS-flagged; 643,975 enforcement). monitoring 964,897 water features. measured PFAS is Maine-only: 117,320 samples over 16 counties, county means to 1,192 ng/L (max 480,000) — 100–300× the 4 ng/L limit. Facility density (per capita) peaks in Permian/Eagle-Ford extraction counties.
Social determinants of health. survey/ranking county poverty (SAIPE), <HS education, food insecurity (County Health Rankings), unemployment, uninsured (ACS/AHRQ), and CDC Social Vulnerability Index — the vulnerability backbone of the score.
Justice. court 684,069 federal cases over 3,122 counties (Cook 113,188; LA 15,439). NIBRS offense charges are national-only (111 categories; disjoint from the court-county key). nikg gun violence (2 counties): Philadelphia 15,205 shootings / 3,163 fatal; Cook 89,367 incidents.
Rural-urban classification. survey/ranking RUCC for 3,221 counties; 1,985 (62%) are nonmetro (RUCC ≥ 4) — the decisive dimension in the high-agreement tail.
Social services. service listing 8,820 substance-use-treatment providers mapped to 2,144 counties (ZIP→place→county); many top-burden counties have zero. DREAM-KG adds 662 Philadelphia services (Mental Health 213, Counseling 192, Food Pantry 140).
Health outcomes. survey/ranking nine CDC PLACES chronic conditions aggregated to 3,057 counties: obesity 37.4%, hypertension 32.6%, depression 23.7%, diabetes 10.5%, asthma 10.6%, COPD 7.5%, coronary disease 5.9%, stroke 3.1%.

Ecological correlations with health & SDoH

Pearson r across ~3,050–3,130 counties. All correlations are ecological (county aggregates), not individual-level or causal.
Social Vulnerability is the strongest correlate of adverse outcomes (diabetes r=0.71, poverty 0.70, food insecurity 0.70, stroke 0.69, low education 0.67). Rurality carries a moderate, consistent health penalty (coronary disease 0.28, poverty 0.26, COPD/obesity 0.22–0.23). Per-capita EPA-facility density correlates negatively with disease (−0.16 to −0.23) — a small-denominator / ecological artifact (density peaks in tiny extraction counties), not a protective effect, and the reason exposure counts and vulnerability rates are scored as separate dimensions.

Coverage by layer

Agreement distribution (0–5) and county coverage per Proto-OKN layer; PFAS is the lone state-limited layer (Maine, 16).
Uncertainties. All correlations are ecological. PFAS is Maine-only (absence elsewhere ≠ absence of PFAS). ufokn urban-flood risk could not be resolved to county within endpoint query limits. nikg = 2 counties and dreamkg = Philadelphia ZIPs are illustrative and excluded from the ranking. NIBRS offense data is national-only. Per-capita rates favor tiny counties, so read the 0–5 agreement as primary. County counts vary by layer (3,052–3,222). Map polygons are standard cartographic boundaries — the only non-Proto-OKN input; every burden/health/social value is from Proto-OKN.

Caveats & reproducibility

Every canonical SPARQL query (verbatim, per layer) is preserved in transcript.md; the assembly/scoring/correlation pipeline is scripts/build_master.py, figures scripts/make_figs.py, map scripts/make_map.py. Re-running each query against the listed KG versions and then the pipeline reproduces every count and correlation. A plain-Markdown version of this report is report.md.
